The readable base arm for the new cases is base-new-cases.log, which runs the head test file against base source and records 7 failed EXIT=1 — every one of the seven new cases fails at base. The negative control ran against working tree over f652394a8a rather than the final head; the only delta to 1c1b41bbf8 is the docs evidence fragment, so the arms are equivalent for code.

findings.text: the census cache key lists regenerate_paths because it 'selects which declared write paths are charged at the reference cost rather than their size', and anchor_paths is the same kind of charge-selecting field, but it is not in the key; a census cached for the unanchored brief is therefore served for the anchored one whenever the file stamps are unchanged, and the anchor silently charges the reference cost anyway. Reproduced in a git-archive extraction of 1c1b41bbf8 with one 1,000,000-byte file: cold cache gives context_census 54392 unanchored and 50392 anchored, while a shared cache dir gives 54392 for both — the anchor's 4000-token saving is absent exactly when a dispatcher previews a brief and then re-dispatches it with --anchor-path, which is the workflow the flag exists for, and the same figure gates the context-fit refusal at routing.py:3545.

both estimate cases call the module-private _context_file_inputs instead of context_census, the function dispatch and the fit verdict actually charge with, so the gate cannot see the census cache key and the blocking defect above passes it green; a case driven through context_census with an unanchored node censused first would have caught it.

_dispatch_request_from_record rebuilds the node field by field and names neither anchor_paths nor regenerate_paths, the same shape the node repaired in queue_admission.py:197, so a node rebuilt from a live run record carries no anchor and any re-estimate through it charges the anchored path at the reference cost.
